scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript validators for a signup form: name (required, non-empty), email (must contain @), age (must be >= 18). Run ALL validators and return ALL errors at once, not just the first one.
criteria: Uses Validate (not Either) so errors accumulate instead of short-circuiting
Uses .combine() to merge results from multiple validators
Returns all errors, not just the first one that fails

scenarios.prompt: Write a DTO validator for CreateProductDto: name (non-empty string), price (positive number), stock (non-negative integer). Each validator should return a typed FieldError object with a field name and message. Accumulate ALL errors.
criteria: Uses Validate.valid() and Validate.invalid() with typed error objects
Error type includes a field name (not just a plain string)
Uses .combine() or sequenceValidate to collect all errors from all fields

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: validate an array of numbers where each must be positive and less than 1000. Return ALL numbers that fail with their index and reason. Use sequenceValidate.
criteria: Uses sequenceValidate to validate all items
Does not short-circuit: all items are validated even after the first failure
Returns errors from all failing items, not just the first
